# SettingRow

SettingRow — puts a setting's name and one-line description at the start and its control (`Toggle`, compact `Select`, or `Button`) at the end, top-aligned to the label. Any `status` (`StatusTag`) sits beside the label so the end slot holds only the action. The row's `label` names `control` through `aria-labelledby`; controls that carry their own visible action text (such as a `Disconnect` `Button`) combine their own id with the row label id so both the action and the setting name are announced.

**Import:** `import { SettingRow } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/SettingRow/SettingRow.jsx`

## Usage

Use `SettingRow` on settings and preference pages where each row adjusts one independent setting or external connection that takes effect immediately. Stack related rows directly under a section heading: adjacent `SettingRow` elements divide with a `1px` border at `--setting-row-pad-y` (`12px`) vertical padding, with no card per row.

## Motion

SettingRow reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Row state and inline control transitions. |

## Alternatives

- For fields edited and submitted together with a Save button, use stacked form fields inside `Fieldset` (see Forms).
- For an option inside a submitted form, use `Checkbox` rather than `Toggle` or `SettingRow`.
- For one value on a record page read far more often than edited, use `InlineEdit`.

## Best practices

### Omit Toggle's own label inside SettingRow. {#omit-toggle-s-own-label-inside-settingrow}

`SettingRow` wires its `label` to `control` through `aria-labelledby`. Passing a second `label` on `Toggle` repeats the text visually and at the end of the row.

Do: Row label at the start names the bare Toggle at the end.
Don't: Toggle repeats its own label in the end slot.

### Put connection status beside the label, never in the control slot. {#put-connection-status-beside-the-label-never-in-the-control-slot}

Pass `StatusTag` through `status` so every row's end slot holds only its action control.

Do: StatusTag sits beside the label; Disconnect stands alone at the end.
Don't: Status crowds the action at the end of the row.

### State the reason in description when a setting is disabled. {#state-the-reason-in-description-when-a-setting-is-disabled}

When a setting waits on another setting on the same page, explain how to unlock it in `description` rather than hiding it in a tooltip.

Do: Description names the prerequisite on the same page.
Don't: Disabled control gives no clue why it cannot be changed.

## Accessibility

- **Label names the control.** `SettingRow` links its `label` span to `control` via `aria-labelledby`, so a `Toggle` announces `"Session reminders, switch, on"` without needing its own visible label, and `status` text beside the label does not pollute the switch's accessible name.
- **Self-describing action buttons.** When `control` carries visible action text (such as a `Disconnect` `Button`), `SettingRow` combines the button's own id with the row label id in `aria-labelledby` (`"Disconnect Google Calendar"`), keeping multiple connection rows distinct for screen-reader users while satisfying WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name.
- **Readable descriptions and announced errors.** `description` and `error` link to `control` via `aria-describedby`; `error` renders with `role="alert"` and sets `aria-invalid="true"`.
- **DOM order matches reading order.** Label, status, description, and inline error precede the end control in the DOM so Tab and virtual-cursor order match visual reading order.

## Related

- `Toggle`: use as `control` when a setting turns on or off and applies immediately.
- `Select`: use with `spacing="compact"` as `control` when a setting picks one option from a short list.
- `StatusTag`: pass to `status` to show connection or feature state beside the setting name.
- `Flag`: use in `FlagGroup` to confirm background saves on a settings page.

## Parts

1. **Label (`label`) and status (`status`).** Strong `--body-default` setting name at the start, with an optional `StatusTag` beside it so the end slot holds only the interactive control.
2. **Description (`description`).** One line of `--body-small` subtle context under the label, or the visible prerequisite/permission reason when disabled or read-only.
3. **Inline error (`error`).** Optional danger error message rendered directly under `description` when a background save fails.
4. **Control (`control` at `end`).** Top-aligned to the label row: a `Toggle` (with no `label` prop), a compact `Select` (`spacing="compact"`), or a compact `Button`.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | `--body-default` medium label in `--ds-text`, `--body-small` description in `--ds-text-subtle`, and control at the end. |
| Saving | `Toggle` sets `isLoading`, showing its saving spinner and `aria-busy="true"` while the request completes. |
| Saved | Change takes effect immediately and confirms via a `Flag` in `FlagGroup`. |
| Error | `error` renders under `description` with `role="alert"` in `--ds-text-danger` and sets `aria-invalid="true"` on the control. |
| Disabled | Label dims to `--ds-text-disabled` and the control disables; `description` keeps `--ds-text-subtle` so the reason stays readable. |
| Read-only | Full contrast and keyboard focus preserved; value controls receive `isReadOnly` and ignore changes. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Row vertical padding and gap | `--setting-row-pad-y` (`12px`), horizontal gap `--inline-lg`. |
| Row divider | `--border-default` solid `--ds-border` between adjacent rows. |
| Label and status | `--body-default` with `--type-weight-medium` in `--ds-text` (`--ds-text-disabled` when disabled); status gap `--inline-md`. |
| Description and error | `--body-small` in `--ds-text-subtle`; error in `--ds-text-danger` with `--icon-sm` glyph. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the setting as a noun phrase: "Session reminders", "Reminder lead time". | Phrase the row label as a question or command with punctuation. |
| Keep `description` to one sentence adding context the label does not already say. | Restate the label ("Turn session reminders on or off"). |
| Write `error` with cause and next step: "Could not save SMS alerts. Check your connection and try again." | "Save failed" or "Error". |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `label` | node (required) | — | The setting's name. Names `control` through `aria-labelledby`. |
| `description` | node | — | One line of context under the label, or the visible reason when disabled or read-only. |
| `control` | node | — | The setting's control at the end: a `Toggle` (with no own label), a compact `Select`, or a `Button`. |
| `status` | node | — | Optional `StatusTag` shown beside `label`, never inside the control slot. |
| `error` | node | — | Inline error message shown under `description` when saving or changing the setting fails. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | `false` | Dims the setting label and forwards `isDisabled` to `control` while keeping `description` readable as the reason. |
| `isReadOnly` | bool | `false` | Marks the setting read-only and forwards `isReadOnly` to value controls. |
| `id` | string | — | Optional id on the row container; also prefixes the generated label and description ids. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class names added to the row container. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline style on the row container. |
| `testId` | string | — | Maps to `data-testid`, for test queries. |
